# Compliance map statuses

Every row of every map carries exactly one of these statuses. They are defined once, in `spec/witness_dictionary.json` (`compliance_map_status`), and describe a SecuraCV mechanism, never a deployment's standing under a regime. The frame: [README.md](README.md).

| Status | Meaning | What a row must carry |
|---|---|---|
| **structural** | A SecuraCV mechanism in code produces this property, and a named test in this tree fails if it regresses. | `test`, `code` |
| **procedural** | A person must do this. SecuraCV supplies the procedure, template or record to do it with; where the software provides nothing, the row names the tracker item and what the deployment does instead. | `procedure`, `operator_action` |
| **designed** | Specified in a design record; not built. The named PR builds it. | `design`, `depends_on` |
| **not-applicable** | The requirement addresses a kind of system SecuraCV is not, or an act no software performs. | `reason` |
| **not-pursued** | SecuraCV deliberately does not provide this; the decision is recorded where the row points. | `reason`, `decision` |

## Crosswalk

How the status words of the ceremony runbook and the Custody Practice Statement template map onto these.

| Document | Its word | Map status |
|---|---|---|
| CEREMONY_RUNBOOK | CODE | structural |
| CEREMONY_RUNBOOK | PROC | procedural |
| CEREMONY_RUNBOOK | GAP | procedural with a tracker evidence entry when the deployment does something instead, designed when a design record exists, not-pursued when declined |
| CPS | shipped | structural |
| CPS | procedural | procedural |
| CPS | not provided | the same three as GAP |
